title: Full frog chorus reports had no clear common warmth slope in eight US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested the link between survey-night temperature and full chorus reports for spring peeper and green frog. We used 23,032 detected species-stop records from 3,558 runs on 324 US routes in 2001-2015. Eight separate species, region and period models controlled site, observer, survey window, route-year, season and reported weather. No slope passed a Holm correction for eight tests. Northeast spring peeper slopes were positive in both periods, but the later slope was uncertain without 2012. Midwest slopes did not repeat that pattern. Missing rain reports limited the Midwest sample to Indiana and Iowa, with only Indiana in the early period. This is a conditional report outcome, not a population estimate or a causal climate effect. Few years, selected nights, sparse full choruses and detection selection limit the tests. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and external data retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Full-chorus probability slopes among detected frogs. Bars are marginal 95 percent route and year cluster intervals. None passes the eight-test Holm correction. MW means Indiana in the early period and Indiana plus Iowa in the later period.
